title: State vs. Appellant (Criminal Appeal)
query_text: The present appeal challenges the judgment of the High Court confirming the conviction of the appellant under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). similar_precedents.text_preview: The appellant was convicted under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code for the murder of his wife. The prosecution relied entirely on circumstantial evidence and the 'last seen together' theory. However, the Supreme Court noted that the chain of circumstances was not complete. There was a significant time gap between when they were last seen and the discovery of the body. The conviction was set aside and the appellant was acquitted.

The petitioner seeks quashing of an FIR registered under Sections 420 and 406 IPC for criminal breach of trust and cheating related to a corporate investment scheme. The Court observed that the dispute is purely civil in nature, arising from a breach of contract regarding corporate funds, and civil remedies were already being pursued. To prevent abuse of process, the FIR is quashed.
